title: AI-guided proof search solves five open problems in Banach space theory
summary: A research project used ChatGPT 5.5 Pro and Codex agents to develop proof ideas and proofs for five Banach-space problems. The resulting paper gives affirmative solutions to questions on toroidal Elton–Odell separation, non-Calkin unital Banach algebras, strict cosingularity and adjoints, weakly compact basis factorization, and primariness of Lp(L1). The authors report that models generated the core mathematics; human mathematicians checked and refined the proofs. The results are presented in an unrefereed preprint, and the authors take responsibility for correctness.
ai_technology: ChatGPT 5.5 Pro and Codex agents using an automated open-problem search pipeline

evidence.tested: A research project used ChatGPT 5.5 Pro and Codex agents to develop proof ideas and proofs for five Banach-space problems.
evidence.unknown: Unrefereed arXiv preprint. Authors state that humans verified and refined the proofs and are responsible for correctness; the proofs are not formally machine-checked. The five problems were selected by mathematicians, while a separate pipeline component automatically found other candidate problems. The five results remain bundled as one paper-level report.
evidence.ai_role: In the pipeline component, agents searched arXiv literature for open problems and attempted solutions. For the five selected Banach-space problems, the authors say model attempts generated the proof ideas and essentially complete arguments before human verification, editing and integration; models were not limited to exposition.
